text.p: Follwing are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Oil company Shell will begin exploration drilling in the Norwegian Sea in the summer. The company hopes to find an oilfield with extractable reserves worth up to 150 billion crowns. Ray Woods, head of Norske Shell, says the Vega prospect will either hold huge oil reserves or nothing at all, but all indicators points to a new discovery.
- Police prevented eight stowaways on a Swedish-registered ship to come ashore at Karmoey in western Norway.

- A new prison at Ringerike is inviting journalists to stay behind bars for one day in February. Journalists have criticised the prison for being luxurious. Those who accept the invitation to "serve their sentence" will be treated as regular prisoners.

- The Nordic electricity bourse, Nord Pool, wants to make it obligatory for companies to inform the market of sensitive information such as on Oslo's stock exchange. Market director Torill Berdal says Nord Pool is considering how the electricity bourse will sanction violations of the regulations.

- Denver-based company Commercial Space Management filed a lawsuit in late December against Boeing Co. and its partners in the satellite-launching venture Sea Launch. The company seeking more than $3 billion in damages for alleged tampering of a contract. Norwegian offshore and engineering company Kvaerner ASA is among the partners Sea Launch.
